hero.title: A coding agent that lives
hero.titleAccent: in your IDE and on your desktop
hero.lead: FoxxyCode brings a full agent into VS Code, JetBrains IDEs and a native Windows window: chat, plans, inline diffs you accept or reject in the editor, the IDE's open files and terminal in context, a browser the agent can drive, and a Russian or English interface. about.title: What FoxxyCode is
paragraphs: FoxxyCode is a fork of [coddy-agent](https://github.com/coddy-project/coddy-agent), a general-purpose agent harness in one static Go binary. It keeps everything upstream has — the ReAct loop, sessions, MCP, rules, skills, subagents, hooks, the scheduler, memory, the swarm — and follows upstream closely.

What the fork adds is the part you touch every day: plugins that make the agent a native citizen of VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, a desktop window for Windows, and agent capabilities that matter inside a real project — inline diff review, the IDE's context, SVN, a browser tool, document export, and a complete Russian interface.

features.title: What the fork adds
features.lead: Everything below exists in FoxxyCode and not in upstream coddy-agent. The full list, with links to the code, is in the documentation.

items.title: VS Code and JetBrains plugins
items.text: One agent process per project, started by the plugin with the binary it bundles. The panel follows the IDE's theme and language.

items.title: Inline diffs in the editor
items.text: Each file the agent edits opens with green and red lines and Accept, Reject, Revert or Show diff, instead of a separate diff pane.

items.title: The IDE's context in the prompt
items.text: Open tabs and the active file, readable `.vscode` and `.idea` project settings, and the terminal output reach the model; `@terminal` quotes it explicitly.

items.title: Drag a file into the chat
items.text: Dropping a file from the project tree adds a short `@` mention, while the model gets the full relative path.

items.title: Native desktop window
items.text: `foxxycode-desktop.exe` hosts the UI in WebView2: no browser tab, no console windows flashing over it.

items.title: Notifications, tour and folders
items.text: Toasts and a chime when a permission prompt or a plan waits for you, a guided first-run tour, and projects opened as folders.

items.title: Interactive browser tool
items.text: The agent opens pages in real Chrome, clicks, fills and scrolls, and sees screenshots — or page text when the model has no vision.

items.title: Subversion on a par with git
items.text: An SVN working copy gets its own branch and revision chip and a set of `svn_*` tools the agent drives directly.

items.title: Export to PDF, DOCX, HTML and JSON
items.text: A session becomes a real document: tables, highlighted code, task lists and the images of the session.

items.title: Debug mode and diagnostics
items.text: A `debug` profile that investigates the root cause before proposing a fix, and an opt-in trace of every request to the model.

items.title: Automatic compaction
items.text: Long conversations are summarized to stay inside the context window, on by default.

items.title: MCP behind a self-signed certificate
items.text: A per-server switch to ignore certificate errors, so an internal MCP server is reachable at all.

items.title: Windows hardened
items.text: Child processes without console windows, honest process termination, Cyrillic SVN output decoded correctly, a running turn rejoined after a reload.

items.title: Russian interface, settings included
items.text: The whole UI in Russian or English, including the generated settings form, switched in Appearance.

items.title: Vision detected from the catalog
items.text: Whether a model accepts images is filled in from the provider's catalog instead of silently staying off.

inherited.title: Inherited from coddy-agent
inherited.text: The harness underneath: one static Go binary, the terminal console, ACP for Zed and other editors, the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, MCP, rules and `AGENTS.md`, skills, subagents, hooks, background tasks, the cron scheduler, long-term memory, the swarm relay and a Telegram gateway.

compareTeaser.title: How FoxxyCode compares
compareTeaser.lead: Twenty-five harnesses and IDE agents side by side, Coddy among them: what they are written in, where you can talk to them, how you extend them, what they do with a long session, what stops them, and how they live in an IDE.
points: In this set, FoxxyCode is the only open harness that ships as a single static binary and also has native VS Code and JetBrains plugins and a desktop app.
It keeps everything Coddy carries in that binary — the web UI, the scheduler, memory, the swarm and a messenger gateway.
Where it loses: no kernel sandbox, no LSP, and file checkpoints only through the IDE's inline diffs.

items.q: How is FoxxyCode related to Coddy?
items.a: FoxxyCode is a fork of [coddy-agent](https://github.com/coddy-project/coddy-agent), MIT-licensed like upstream. It regularly ports upstream changes and adds IDE plugins, the desktop app and the capabilities listed above. If you want the agent in a container, a terminal or Telegram without the IDE story, upstream Coddy at [coddy.dev](https://coddy.dev) may be all you need.

VS Code 1.75 or newer, and JetBrains IDEs on the IntelliJ platform from 2022.2 on: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider and the rest. Other editors can host the agent over ACP with `foxxycode acp`.

items.q: Is the plugin on the VS Code Marketplace or JetBrains Marketplace?
items.a: Not yet. The VS Code extension installs from the `.vsix`. The JetBrains plugin comes from its own plugin repository, so after you add the address once the IDE installs and updates it like any marketplace plugin.

items.q: Which models does it work with?
items.a: Any OpenAI-compatible API plus Anthropic: OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, NeuralDeep or your own gateway, always with your keys. With a local model no prompt leaves your machine.

items.q: Is the desktop app available for macOS or Linux?
items.a: The desktop window is Windows-only for now. On macOS and Linux use the plugins, the web UI (`foxxycode http`) or the console; builds for both are on the releases page.

items.q: Do I need to install Go or Node?
items.a: No. Every package ships a prebuilt binary. Go, Node and a JDK are only needed to build the plugins from source.

compare.title: FoxxyCode vs the 2026 agent harnesses
compare.lead: Twenty-five harnesses and IDE agents side by side: what they are written in, where you can talk to them, how you extend them, what happens to a long session, what stops them from running something you did not ask for, and how they fit into an IDE. FoxxyCode is one row among them, and so is Coddy, the project it forks.
compare.compiled: Compiled in September 2026. FoxxyCode was read from its own source at 0.2.93. The twenty rows shared with the [Coddy comparison](https://coddy.dev/compare/) start from that page and were checked against each project's documentation, which updated several of them; FoxxyCode, Kilo Code, Roo Code, Continue and Cursor were added from their own documentation. Sources are at the bottom.

camps.title: How the field splits
paragraphs: **Lab agents** — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity, Grok Build — come from the model vendors and set the conventions everyone else adopts: `AGENTS.md`, MCP, skills.
**Open harnesses** — Coddy, OpenCode, Pi, OMP, DeepSeek Harness, Goose, Aider, OpenHands, Crush, Reasonix, CodeWhale — compete on features, mostly in the terminal.
**IDE agents** — Cline, Kilo Code, Roo Code, Continue, Cursor, Koda — live in the editor, where the diff you accept is the unit of work.
**Personal assistants** — OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Drift — build the gateway first and attach the model to it.
FoxxyCode sits between the open harnesses and the IDE agents: Coddy's harness, delivered through the IDE and the desktop.

verdict.title: Where FoxxyCode wins, where it lags

strengthItems.title: A harness inside the IDE, not a separate product
strengthItems.text: Cline, Kilo Code and Continue started as IDE extensions. FoxxyCode puts a full harness — scheduler, memory, swarm, hooks, subagents — behind the same panel, and the session you start in the IDE opens in the web UI or the terminal.

strengthItems.title: Both big IDE families, one agent
strengthItems.text: The VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin host the same UI and the same binary, so settings, sessions and skills are shared rather than reimplemented per editor.

strengthItems.title: Review in the editor
strengthItems.text: Agent edits arrive as inline diffs with accept, reject and revert in both IDEs, as in Cline or Kilo Code, but the harness behind them also runs in a terminal, a browser or a container.

strengthItems.title: Windows as a first-class platform
strengthItems.text: A native desktop window, no console flashes, Cyrillic-safe SVN output. Most harnesses treat Windows as an afterthought.

strengthItems.title: A Russian interface
strengthItems.text: The UI, the settings form and the plugin change notes exist in Russian as well as English.

gapItems.title: No kernel-level sandbox
gapItems.text: Protection comes from the permission gate, the modes and, when you want it, a container. Codex CLI enforces Landlock, seccomp and Seatbelt in the process.

gapItems.title: No LSP
gapItems.text: The agent reads files as text; OpenCode and OMP wire a language server into every edit.

gapItems.title: No marketplace listing
gapItems.text: Cline, Kilo Code and Continue install from the VS Code and JetBrains marketplaces in one click; FoxxyCode needs a `.vsix` or a plugin repository address.

gapItems.title: Desktop on Windows only
gapItems.text: Cline, Goose, Claude Code and Koda have desktop apps on more systems.

gapItems.title: A small community
gapItems.text: Orders of magnitude fewer users than the popular IDE agents, so fewer shared skills and fewer eyes on edge cases.

pick.title: When to pick which
paragraphs: **Pick FoxxyCode** when you want one agent in VS Code, a JetBrains IDE and a desktop window at once, with your own models, sessions that move between those surfaces, inline review of every edit, and an interface in Russian.
**Pick Coddy** when the agent should live in a container, a terminal or Telegram and the IDE plugins are not the point — it is the same harness without the fork's additions.

**Pick something else** when a marketplace install and a large community matter most (Cline, Kilo Code), when you want an AI-first editor rather than a plugin (Cursor), or when unfamiliar code must run under a kernel sandbox (Codex CLI).
